steps.message:
# Some coins misbehave in the flooded cave

### What happens
`recording.mp4` is an uncut run through a flooded cave basin. Partway through the clip, Tux does something that releases a group of new coins. From that moment until the end of the clip, those coins do not behave the way coins in this game should. The coins that were already placed in the level, Tux, the fish and the scenery in the recording are correct.

### Expected
The released coins should behave like a normal coin burst in this game, from the moment they spread out of the block until they come to rest and Tux collects them. Once a coin is in the water it should drift down slowly. Fix every way the released coins behave wrongly in the recording.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4` (44 seconds)

You can inspect individual moments of the video by extracting frames from it with `ffmpeg`.

Inspect the attached file before making changes.

I fixed three problems in how the coins from a coin-burst block behave. The build succeeds, but I haven't run the game to watch the result.

**I couldn't watch the recording.** `/app/.harbor_assets/` is empty and there's no `recording.mp4` anywhere on the system. So I worked out the bugs from the code instead. When a block releases a "group of new coins", the bonus block creates a `CoinExplode` (`src/object/bonus_block.cpp:472`), and that throws ten `HeavyCoin`s.

**What I fixed:**

1. **The burst went the wrong way** (`src/object/coin_explode.cpp`). The left/right sign was applied to the vertical speed instead of the horizontal one. As a result, every coin flew to the same side, and half of them shot downward instead of arcing up. Now the coins spread in a fan to both sides, five to the left and five to the right, all thrown upward.

2. **The coins never came to rest** (`HeavyCoin::collision_solid` in `src/object/coin.cpp`).
   - Any coin landing faster than 20 px/s bounced, so the coins kept hopping. I raised the cutoff to 200 px/s, so only hard landings bounce.
   - When a coin landed, its sideways speed was never cleared, so it slid along the floor forever. It now stops dead.

3. **The coins ignored water** (`HeavyCoin::update`). They fell through water at full speed. Now, while a coin overlaps a water tile, gravity drops to 20% and its movement is slowed (×0.4 sideways, ×0.6 downward), so it drifts down slowly. I copied these values from the rocks, which already behave this way in water.

The coins already placed in the level, Tux and the fish run on different code, which I didn't touch. Because I didn't have the recording, a quick playtest of a coin-burst block over water would confirm the burst now matches what you expect.
